instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll restore order in this meeting. Your apology needs to cover interrupting the chair, as well as the spilled tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The trousers can wait. Use whatever words feel natural, but I need the chair's position respected.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll apologize quietly. I'm not making a speech about it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quietly is fine. Lean this way and say you shouldn't have interrupted the chair. Then I'll thank you and we can continue as a cooperative meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still leading tomorrow's training. You called their head trainer an idiot; I need you to apologize for undermining that position.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the drill went badly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not the drill, the head trainer. Put it in your own words; I want the trainees and us working together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email them tonight. I won't stand up and give a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An email is fine. Send it before the drill and let me read the apology aloud at the start. I'll use your wording. My first instruction needs to sound like it comes from their trainer again.

cards.title: Secure the Endorsement
cards.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lead the rota presentation. Back my decision into this microphone so the staff can hear we're together on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already told you it's fine. I don't want to make a speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A sentence in your own words will do. I just need support that reaches the people who'll challenge it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email you instead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Email is ideal. You choose the wording; copy the whole team and I'll present it alongside the rota. Then it's our supported decision, not just my bright idea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm taking our extension proposal to the neighbors. Sign your support here so they can see I'm not speaking alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the extension. I don't want my full name on the page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep it discreet. What mark would you be comfortable putting beside your support?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Initials it is. I'll use the same size. Could we put the household names in a small key below? You choose where; I need them to know which support is yours when the objections start.

cards.title: Delegate Downward
cards.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As junior coordinator, you'll deal with the blocked sink. I'll keep the event running.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran yesterday's event. You promised me a promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Senior coordinator, then. Still reporting to me, but you can choose the plumber and supervise the repair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The only one available comes after everyone leaves. I'm not waiting here hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll order whatever dinner you want. You hold the building keys and lock up after him; senior site responsibility. Tell me the delivery time and I'll arrange the handover around you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're my deputy, so you'll answer the inspector's complaints. I'll stay at the decision-making level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're complaints about decisions you made.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you'll have my notes. Use your own wording for the replies; deputies handle the detailed explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The signer has to attend tomorrow's hearing. I'm not facing it alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll come and supply any facts you need. You sign and speak as deputy; I'll be there as your superior. Choose where I sit so you can turn to me. We can keep the hierarchy clear and work together.

cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll coordinate the trip booking. Before I commit us, who could still stop it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. Please book before we lose the coach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep the booking moving. Just tell me whose objection could stop the deposit; you can give me the short version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's, but she's away. Her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we'll use your route. Can the deputy release the money alone, or does she need the treasurer's say-so? You make the introduction however suits you; I'll take the call from there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get this pipe repair moving. Which signatures release the money?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All three. I've spent the whole morning getting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good work. I won't send you round again. Is there anyone who can still freeze the payment after those signatures?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance. They unfroze the roof money when the caretaker called, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll follow that up myself. Does the caretaker overrule finance, or know the person who can? Just point me to the right door; I'll handle the explanation and let you get back to your day.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lead the allotment shed proposal. Sit beside me for the vote so they can see this is more than my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if every plot holder gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shared keys will be my opening promise. You can explain how access works; I want us presenting together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that before they'll sit with us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you introduce me to them, and let them choose where we all sit. I'll build the proposal around shared access. I'd rather lead a full row than defend an empty seat beside me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lead a request to keep the pottery room open late. Join me so it looks like a users' proposal, not a favor for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I leave at five. Late opening does nothing for my class.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what your class needs. I can lead a broader proposal; I want you beside me when we present it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Weekend access. Two of the morning students would come if that's included.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include it. You and those two can explain weekends first; I'll follow with evenings. We'll present as the room users, and I'll fit the request around all our classes.
